_comment: What this domain's data looks like on disk. Infrastructure reads this to recognise and load it; it does not know the shapes itself, in the same way it does not know what any capability computes.
label: Spatial Transcriptomics
notes: Tumour samples measured with position kept: which regions a tissue breaks into, and which genes differ between neighbouring regions.
_input_label_note: What to call this domain's data where it is shown beside the results computed from it, such as the first column of the versions grid. The word people here use for the thing every analysis starts from, which is more use to them than the word 'data'.
_datasets_note: Three shapes, because the same science exists at three stages and the output of one stage is the input of the next. Declared most specific first. A folder is whichever shape it fits best, so a Space Ranger run is not mistaken for a bare tree of directories.

datasets.label: A Space Ranger run
datasets.notes: Raw output from the instrument's own pipeline. The only place the tissue image and its scale factors exist, so anything that draws on tissue has to come back here.

datasets.label: Harmonised samples
datasets.notes: One folder per sample, each holding the densified matrix and its labels. What the spatial capabilities read. Where the instrument's own run was kept for a sample it sits beside them, under instrument_run, and it is the only place the tissue image and its scale factors exist. A sample can carry both: the run is not a stage a sample leaves behind, and its absence means it was never brought here rather than that it was used up.

datasets.label: A study of samples
datasets.notes: A sample tree with optional root tables: a cohort index and a gene symbol map.

versioned_note: The same pipeline is run over every sample of a study and rerun as parameters settle, so one question has several answers and a person has to say which is in play. Domains that say nothing here are not asked, and their clients do not offer the choice.
